patterns.T6: Order, rate law, units of k

U1.name: Solutions (7 marks)
U1.tip: Colligative numericals: ΔT_f = iK_f m, ΔT_b = iK_b m, π = iCRT; molar mass M = K_f × w × 1000/(ΔT_f × W). i = number of ions on complete dissociation. Positive deviation → minimum-boiling azeotrope (ethanol–water). Osmotic pressure suits proteins and polymers.
U1.ncert: NCERT Chemistry Part I/II (Class 12, 2026-27): Unit 1 Solutions

U2.name: Electrochemistry (9 marks)
U2.tip: Nernst: E = E° − (0.059/n) log Q at 298 K. Λm unit S cm² mol⁻¹; weak electrolytes: Λm rises steeply on dilution (α increases), so use Kohlrausch: Λ°(CH₃COOH) = Λ°(HCl) + Λ°(CH₃COONa) − Λ°(NaCl). Faraday: moles of metal = charge (F) ÷ n.
U2.ncert: NCERT Chemistry Part I/II (Class 12, 2026-27): Unit 2 Electrochemistry

U3.name: Chemical Kinetics (7 marks)
U3.tip: First order: t½ = 0.693/k, unit of k = s⁻¹; 75% done = 2 half-lives. Rate law exponents come from experiment: rate = k[A]ˣ[B]ʸ. Pseudo first order when one reactant is in large excess (ester hydrolysis in water).
U3.ncert: NCERT Chemistry Part I/II (Class 12, 2026-27): Unit 3 Chemical Kinetics

U4.name: d- and f-Block Elements (7 marks)
U4.tip: Spin-only μ = √(n(n + 2)) BM (Mn²⁺ d⁵ → 5.92). Zn, Cd, Hg: full d¹⁰ in ground state and common oxidation state, so not typical transition metals. Lanthanoid contraction makes Zr and Hf almost the same size.
U4.ncert: NCERT Chemistry Part I/II (Class 12, 2026-27): Unit 4 The d- and f-Block Elements

U5.name: Coordination Compounds (7 marks)
U5.tip: IUPAC: ligands alphabetically, then metal with oxidation state in Roman numerals. CN⁻ is a strong-field ligand → low spin ([Fe(CN)₆]³⁻ has 1 unpaired e⁻; [Ni(CN)₄]²⁻ is dsp², square planar, diamagnetic). NO₂⁻ / ONO⁻ → linkage isomers.
U5.ncert: NCERT Chemistry Part I/II (Class 12, 2026-27): Unit 5 Coordination Compounds

U6.name: Haloalkanes and Haloarenes (6 marks)
U6.tip: SN2: CH₃X > 1° > 2° > 3°, one step, inversion. SN1: 3° fastest, racemisation. Finkelstein: R–Cl/Br + NaI in dry acetone → R–I. Haloarenes resist nucleophilic substitution: C–X has partial double-bond character (resonance).
U6.ncert: NCERT Chemistry Part I/II (Class 12, 2026-27): Unit 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

U7.name: Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers (6 marks)
U7.tip: Acidity: o/p-nitrophenol > phenol > alcohols (−NO₂ stabilises phenoxide). Reimer-Tiemann: phenol + CHCl₃/NaOH → salicylaldehyde. Williamson: use the bulky alkoxide with a primary (methyl) halide; a 3° halide gives elimination.
U7.ncert: NCERT Chemistry Part I/II (Class 12, 2026-27): Unit 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

U8.name: Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids (8 marks)
U8.tip: Clemmensen (Zn-Hg/HCl) and Wolff-Kishner turn C=O into CH₂. Iodoform test needs CH₃CO– (or CH₃CH(OH)–). Tollens' test separates aldehydes (incl. benzaldehyde) from ketones. Cannizzaro needs an aldehyde with no α-H. Electron-withdrawing groups raise acid strength (FCH₂COOH strongest).
U8.ncert: NCERT Chemistry Part I/II (Class 12, 2026-27): Unit 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids

U9.name: Amines (6 marks)
U9.tip: Basicity in water (ethyl series): 2° > 3° > 1° > NH₃. Hofmann bromamide: amide → amine with one carbon less. Aniline gives no Friedel-Crafts reaction: it forms a salt with AlCl₃. Carbylamine test = 1° amines only.
U9.ncert: NCERT Chemistry Part I/II (Class 12, 2026-27): Unit 9 Amines

U10.name: Biomolecules (7 marks)
U10.tip: Glucose + HI → n-hexane (six-carbon straight chain). DNA: deoxyribose, A G C T; RNA: ribose, A G C U. Denaturation destroys 2° and 3° structure but keeps the 1° sequence. Vitamin C deficiency → scurvy; D → rickets.
U10.ncert: NCERT Chemistry Part I/II (Class 12, 2026-27): Unit 10 Biomolecules

questions.question: 2 g of a non-electrolyte dissolved in 100 g of benzene lowers its freezing point by 0.512 K. K_f of benzene is 5.12 K kg mol⁻¹. Find the molar mass of the solute, in g mol⁻¹.

questions.question: What is the van 't Hoff factor i for K₂SO₄, assuming complete dissociation in water?
questions.explanation: K₂SO₄ → 2K⁺ + SO₄²⁻: three ions, so i = 3.

questions.explanation: Ethanol–water shows large positive deviation; about 95% ethanol forms a minimum-boiling azeotrope.

Negative deviation and forms a maximum-boiling azeotrope
Positive deviation and forms a maximum-boiling azeotrope

questions.question: Choose the correct option.

questions.question: The unit of molar conductivity commonly used in NCERT tables is:
questions.explanation: Λm = κ/c, so S cm⁻¹ ÷ mol cm⁻³ = S cm² mol⁻¹.
questions.remediation: Electrochemistry (9 marks): NCERT Chemistry Part I/II (Class 12, 2026-27): Unit 2 Electrochemistry; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: How many moles of copper are deposited at the cathode when 4 faradays of charge pass through CuSO₄ solution?
questions.explanation: Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu: 2 F deposit 1 mol, so 4 F deposit 2 mol.
questions.remediation: Electrochemistry (9 marks): NCERT Chemistry Part I/II (Class 12, 2026-27): Unit 2 Electrochemistry; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: For a cell reaction with n = 2, E°cell = 0.300 V and the reaction quotient Q = 100 at 298 K. Using E = E° − (0.059/n) log Q, find E_cell in millivolts.
questions.remediation: Electrochemistry (9 marks): NCERT Chemistry Part I/II (Class 12, 2026-27): Unit 2 Electrochemistry; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: Λ°m for HCl, CH₃COONa and NaCl are 425.9, 91.0 and 126.4 S cm² mol⁻¹. Λ°m for CH₃COOH is:
questions.explanation: Kohlrausch: Λ°(CH₃COOH) = Λ°(HCl) + Λ°(CH₃COONa) − Λ°(NaCl) = 425.9 + 91.0 − 126.4 = 390.5.
questions.remediation: Electrochemistry (9 marks): NCERT Chemistry Part I/II (Class 12, 2026-27): Unit 2 Electrochemistry; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: Choose the correct option.

questions.question: The unit of the rate constant of a first-order reaction is:
questions.explanation: For first order, k = rate/[A], so (mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹)/(mol L⁻¹) = s⁻¹.
questions.remediation: Chemical Kinetics (7 marks): NCERT Chemistry Part I/II (Class 12, 2026-27): Unit 3 Chemical Kinetics; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: A first-order reaction has k = 0.0693 min⁻¹. What is its half-life, in minutes?
questions.remediation: Chemical Kinetics (7 marks): NCERT Chemistry Part I/II (Class 12, 2026-27): Unit 3 Chemical Kinetics; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: The half-life of a first-order reaction is 20 min. How long (in minutes) does it take for 75% of the reactant to be used up?
questions.explanation: 75% used = 25% left = (1/2)², i.e. 2 half-lives = 40 min.
questions.remediation: Chemical Kinetics (7 marks): NCERT Chemistry Part I/II (Class 12, 2026-27): Unit 3 Chemical Kinetics; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: For the rate law rate = k[A][B]², [A] is halved and [B] is doubled. By what factor does the rate change?
questions.explanation: New rate = k(½[A])(2[B])² = ½ × 4 = 2 times the old rate.
questions.remediation: Chemical Kinetics (7 marks): NCERT Chemistry Part I/II (Class 12, 2026-27): Unit 3 Chemical Kinetics; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: Zn, Cd and Hg are not regarded as typical transition elements because:
questions.explanation: d¹⁰ in the atom and in M²⁺, so no partly filled d orbitals.
questions.remediation: d- and f-Block Elements (7 marks): NCERT Chemistry Part I/II (Class 12, 2026-27): Unit 4 The d- and f-Block Elements; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.
options: They have no d electrons at all
They have completely filled d orbitals in the ground state and in their common oxidation states

questions.question: The spin-only magnetic moment of Mn²⁺ (Z of Mn = 25) is about:
questions.explanation: Mn²⁺ is 3d⁵: n = 5 unpaired, μ = √(5 × 7) = √35 ≈ 5.92 BM.
questions.remediation: d- and f-Block Elements (7 marks): NCERT Chemistry Part I/II (Class 12, 2026-27): Unit 4 The d- and f-Block Elements; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: Zirconium (4d) and hafnium (5d) have almost identical atomic radii because of:
questions.explanation: The poor shielding of 4f electrons cancels the expected size increase from Zr to Hf.
questions.remediation: d- and f-Block Elements (7 marks): NCERT Chemistry Part I/II (Class 12, 2026-27): Unit 4 The d- and f-Block Elements; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: The IUPAC name of [Co(NH₃)₅Cl]Cl₂ is:
questions.explanation: Ligands alphabetical (ammine before chlorido); Co: x − 1 = +2 → x = +3.
questions.remediation: Coordination Compounds (7 marks): NCERT Chemistry Part I/II (Class 12, 2026-27): Unit 5 Coordination Compounds; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: How many unpaired electrons are there in [Fe(CN)₆]³⁻?
questions.explanation: Fe³⁺ is 3d⁵; CN⁻ is strong field, so low spin t₂g⁵: one unpaired electron.
questions.remediation: Coordination Compounds (7 marks): NCERT Chemistry Part I/II (Class 12, 2026-27): Unit 5 Coordination Compounds; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: Which complex is square planar and diamagnetic?
questions.explanation: Ni²⁺ (d⁸) with strong-field CN⁻ pairs up electrons: dsp², square planar, no unpaired electrons. [NiCl₄]²⁻ is tetrahedral and paramagnetic.
questions.remediation: Coordination Compounds (7 marks): NCERT Chemistry Part I/II (Class 12, 2026-27): Unit 5 Coordination Compounds; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: [Co(NH₃)₅(NO₂)]Cl₂ and [Co(NH₃)₅(ONO)]Cl₂ are:
questions.explanation: The ambidentate NO₂⁻ binds through N (nitro) in one and O (nitrito) in the other.
questions.remediation: Coordination Compounds (7 marks): NCERT Chemistry Part I/II (Class 12, 2026-27): Unit 5 Coordination Compounds; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: R–Cl + NaI in dry acetone → R–I + NaCl. This is the:
questions.explanation: Halide exchange with NaI in dry acetone is the Finkelstein reaction (NaCl precipitates).
questions.remediation: Haloalkanes and Haloarenes (6 marks): NCERT Chemistry Part I/II (Class 12, 2026-27): Unit 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: Which compound reacts fastest by the SN2 mechanism?
questions.explanation: SN2 is fastest for the least hindered carbon: methyl > 1° > 2° > 3°.
questions.remediation: Haloalkanes and Haloarenes (6 marks): NCERT Chemistry Part I/II (Class 12, 2026-27): Unit 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: Which is the correct order of acid strength?
questions.explanation: −NO₂ at para stabilises the phenoxide ion; alcohols are weaker acids than phenol.

questions.question: Phenol treated with chloroform and aqueous NaOH, followed by acid, gives:

questions.question: Which pair of reactants is best for preparing tert-butyl methyl ether by Williamson synthesis?
questions.explanation: A 3° halide with a strong base gives elimination (an alkene); the SN2 route needs the primary (methyl) halide.
questions.remediation: Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers (6 marks): NCERT Chemistry Part I/II (Class 12, 2026-27): Unit 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: Reduction of a ketone's C=O group to CH₂ with zinc amalgam and concentrated HCl is the:
questions.explanation: Zn-Hg/conc. HCl: Clemmensen; NH₂NH₂/KOH in glycol: Wolff-Kishner.

questions.question: Which compound gives a positive iodoform test?
questions.explanation: The test needs a CH₃CO– group; acetone (propan-2-one) has it.

questions.question: Which is the strongest acid?
questions.explanation: F is the most electronegative, so it stabilises the carboxylate ion most.

questions.question: Which test distinguishes benzaldehyde from acetophenone?
questions.explanation: Aldehydes reduce Tollens' reagent; ketones do not. (Acetophenone gives the iodoform test; benzaldehyde does not.)
questions.remediation: Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids (8 marks): NCERT Chemistry Part I/II (Class 12, 2026-27): Unit 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.
options: Tollens' test: benzaldehyde gives a silver mirror
Iodoform test: benzaldehyde gives a yellow precipitate
Both give a silver mirror with Tollens' reagent
Sodium bicarbonate test: acetophenone gives effervescence

questions.question: Deficiency of vitamin C causes:

questions.question: On prolonged heating with HI, glucose gives n-hexane. This shows that:

questions.question: Which base is present in RNA but not in DNA?

questions.question: When egg white is boiled, the protein coagulates. Which level of protein structure survives?
questions.explanation: Denaturation breaks the H-bonds holding 2° and 3° structures; the peptide-bond sequence (1°) stays intact.
